description: We are GeoVolt, a team of engineering students interested in space technology, Earth science and innovation. We are excited to explore NASA data, analyse environmental changes and develop creative solutions to real-world challenges. Our interests include technology, research, data analysis and problem-solving. We believe in teamwork, learning and sharing ideas to make our project meaningful.
summary: EARTHPULSE is an interactive environmental data analysis platform that identifies and visualizes long-term changes in Earth's environmental systems using NASA satellite observations and scientific models. The application focuses on analyzing land surface temperature, precipitation, vegetation and soil moisture across different geographical regions. Users can select locations, variables and time periods to explore environmental changes through interactive maps, graphs and statistical analysis. Using trend detection methods, including Sen's slope and the Mann-Kendall test, EARTHPULSE estimates the rate of change and evaluates its statistical significance. By integrating Earth observation data with software and engineering concepts, the project aims to make complex environmental trends easier to investigate, compare and understand.
details:
EARTHPULSE is a web-based environmental trend detection platform developed to analyze long-term changes in Earth's environmental systems using NASA satellite observations and scientific datasets.

The platform focuses on four important environmental variables: land surface temperature, precipitation, vegetation and soil moisture.

Users can select a geographical location, choose environmental variables and specify a study period. The system processes the selected data and presents the results through interactive graphs, maps and comparative visualizations.

Statistical methods such as Sen's slope and the Mann-Kendall test are used to identify the direction and rate of environmental changes and evaluate their statistical significance.

The main objective is to identify what is changing, where the changes are occurring, how much change is taking place and whether the observed changes are statistically significant.

The project combines Electrical Engineering concepts, including data processing, numerical analysis and software development, with Civil Engineering concepts such as geographical analysis and environmental assessment.

The proposed system uses Python for data processing and statistical analysis, HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the user interface, and NASA open-access Earth science datasets.

EARTHPULSE aims to make complex environmental data easier to understand and encourage scientific investigation of changes in Earth's interconnected environmental systems.
